extracted.intended_audience: registrants (issuers) and qualified persons preparing technical report summaries and related SEC disclosures (mineral resources/reserves and asset-backed securities certifications)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and disclosure standards for technical report summaries supporting mineral resource, mineral reserve, or exploration result disclosures (Regulation S‑K). Also includes related certification and exhibit requirements for asset-backed issuers and shelf offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13a-14(d)/15d-14(d) Certifications (asset-backed issuers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications required by Rule 13a-14(d) or Rule 15d-14(d) for asset-backed issuers, to be provided exactly as set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes statements that the certifier has reviewed the Exchange Act periodic reports; that, based on knowledge, the reports do not contain any untrue material statement or omit material facts; that distribution, servicing and other information required under Form 10-D is included; statements regarding responsibility for reviewing servicer activities and whether servicers have fulfilled obligations under servicing agreements; inclusion of required reports on assessment of compliance with servicing criteria and disclosure of any material noncompliance. Notes clarify who must sign (senior officer in charge of securitization or servicing as applicable), that a natural person must sign in individual capacity, and which version of paragraph 4 to use when servicer vs depositor signs. If relying on unaffiliated parties' information, include a statement identifying those parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification content: servicer-related disclosures (Rule 13a-14(d)/15d-14(d) detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifier must disclose, based on most recent evaluation, to auditors and audit committee: (a) all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting reasonably likely to adversely affect ability to report financial information, and (b) any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or employees with a significant role in internal control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the officer-level certification language required to be provided; separate certification required for each principal executive and financial officer per Rules 13a-14(a) and 15d-14(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1350 Certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Certifications required by Rule 13a-14(b)/15d-14(b) and 18 U.S.C. 1350 (Section 1350) must be furnished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certification furnished pursuant to this item will not be deemed 'filed' for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act and will not be incorporated by reference into other filings except to the extent specifically incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on assessment of compliance with servicing criteria (Item §229.1122(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report on assessment of compliance with servicing criteria required by §229.1122(a) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This references Regulation AB requirements for including these assessment reports as exhibits to the filing; if a required report is not attached, the Form 10-K must disclose that it is not included and provide an explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation report on assessment of compliance with servicing criteria (Item §229.1122(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each attestation report on assessment of compliance with servicing criteria required by §229.1122(b) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These attestation reports (Rule 13a-18 / 15d-18) must be included as exhibits unless otherwise disclosed; any material instances of noncompliance described in such reports must be disclosed in the Form 10-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Servicer compliance statement (Item §229.1123)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each servicer compliance statement required by §229.1123 must be included in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the signer reasonably relies on information provided by unaffiliated parties (trustees, depositors, servicers, etc.), a paragraph acknowledging that reliance must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification for shelf offerings of asset-backed securities (Form SF-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the certification required by General Instruction I.B.1.(a) of Form SF-3 exactly as set forth, certifying review of the prospectus and knowledge about securitized assets and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must state that the signer has reviewed the prospectus, that it does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit material facts, that the prospectus and registration statement fairly present characteristics/structure/risks of the securitized assets, and that there is a reasonable basis to conclude the securitization is structured to produce expected cash flows (but not guaranteed). The certification is subject to available federal securities law defenses and must be signed by the chief executive officer of the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine Safety Disclosure Exhibit (Item 104 of Regulation S-K)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that is an operator, or has a subsidiary that is an operator, of a coal or other mine must provide the information required by Item 104 of Regulation S-K in an exhibit to its Exchange Act annual or quarterly report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: 'coal or other mine' per Federal Mine Safety and Health Act; 'operator' as defined in that Act; 'subsidiary' per Exchange Act Rule 12b-2. Include required mine safety disclosure items in exhibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical report summary: qualified person requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant disclosing information concerning mineral resources or mineral reserves must file a technical report summary by one or more qualified persons that identifies and summarizes the scientific and technical information and conclusions for each material property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may elect to file a technical report summary that addresses exploration results. The summary must not include large amounts of technical or other project data; the qualified person must draft the summary to conform, to the extent practicable, with plain English principles set forth in §230.421 or §240.13a-20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary (technical report summary item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the most significant information: property description (including mineral rights) and ownership, geology and mineralization, status of exploration/development/operations, mineral resource and reserve estimates, summary capital and operating cost estimates, permitting requirements, and the qualified person's conclusions and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive summary must be brief and should not contain all detailed information from the technical support summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction (technical report summary item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose the registrant for whom the summary was prepared; terms of reference and purpose (reporting resources, reserves, or exploration results); sources of information and data used with citations if applicable; details of the personal inspection on the property by each qualified person or explanation if not inspected; and whether the summary updates a previously filed summary (identify name and date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the purpose and information sources; document inspections or reasons they were not completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property description (technical report summary item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe property location accurate to within one mile using an easily recognizable coordinate system; provide appropriate maps with proper engineering detail legible on the page; disclose area; list title/claim/mineral right/lease/option names or numbers with expiration dates and payments; describe mineral rights acquisition and any conditions to obtain/retain the property; describe significant encumbrances including permitting requirements and timelines; disclose other factors/risks affecting access, title, or ability to perform work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant holds only a royalty or similar interest (except as specified), provide analogous information for the property owner/operator, including documents under which they hold/operate the property and related conditions/encumbrances/risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility, climate, local resources, infrastructure and physiography
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe topography, elevation, vegetation; means of access (highways, towns, rivers, railroads, airports); climate and length of operating season (if applicable); availability of and required infrastructure including sources of water, electricity, personnel, and supplies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail to assess the practical aspects of accessing and operating on the property.

rubrics_metrics.name: History (previous operations and exploration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe previous operations, including names of previous operators where known; describe type, amount, quantity, and general results of exploration and development work undertaken by previous owners/operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide relevant historical context that may affect interpretation of current data and resource assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological setting, mineralization, and deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe regional, local, and property geology and significant mineralized zones, summarize surrounding rock types, relevant geological controls, length/width/depth/continuity of mineralization, and describe type, character, and distribution of the mineralization; identify each mineral deposit type under investigation and the geological model(s) being applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one stratigraphic column and one cross-section of the local geology to meet the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration (scope and reporting requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the nature and extent of all relevant exploration work conducted by or on behalf of the registrant, with specific requirements for non-drilling work, drilling, hydrogeology, geotechnical data, and inclusion of plan view maps showing drill holes and samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-drilling: procedures/parameters, sampling methods and quality, representativeness and potential biases, location/number/type/spacing/density, area covered, and significant results/interpretation. For drilling: type/extent of drilling, procedures, drilling/sampling/recovery factors affecting accuracy, material results/interpretation; for exploration results summaries must include all samples or drill holes or identify omitted information and explain why not material. For hydrogeology and geotechnical: describe sampling, lab techniques, QA/QC, results and interpretations, models and assumptions. Technical report summary must comply with all disclosure standards under §§229.1300–1305. If reporting an exploration target, include a clearly captioned subsection and required disclosure under §229.1302(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample preparation, analyses, and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe sample preparation methods and quality control measures prior to sending samples to labs, sample splitting/reduction methods, security measures to ensure validity/integrity of samples; sample preparation, assaying and analytical procedures used, name/location/relationship of labs and any certifications; nature/extent/results of QA/QC procedures; opinion on adequacy of sample preparation, security, and analytical procedures; and justification if analytical procedures are not conventional industry practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified person must opine on adequacy and explain unconventional procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe steps taken by the qualified person to verify the data: data verification procedures applied; any limitations or failures to conduct verification and reasons; and the qualified person's opinion on the adequacy of the data for the purposes used in the summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about verification methods and any caveats or limitations that affect confidence in the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral processing and metallurgical testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe nature and extent of mineral processing or metallurgical testing and analytical procedures; degree to which test samples are representative; labs used and their relationships/certifications; relevant results including assumptions or predictions about recovery estimates and processing factors or deleterious elements that could affect extraction; and the qualified person's opinion on adequacy of data; if procedures are not conventional, state so and justify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss representativeness and potential impacts on economic extraction; provide justification for nonstandard methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral resource estimates (content and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If included, describe key assumptions, parameters, and methods used to estimate mineral resources in sufficient detail for a reasonably informed person to understand the basis for the estimates; include estimates at a specific point of reference selected by the qualified person; provide estimates for all commodities including quantities, grade/quality, cut-off grades, and recoveries; round off estimates to appropriate significant figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose cut-off grade estimates based on assumed costs and commodity prices with the price used and detailed reasons for the selection including time frame; classify resources into inferred/indicated/measured with criteria and justification; discuss uncertainty sources and how considered, listing all factors; when reporting multiple commodity as equivalents, disclose individual grades and conversion factors; provide qualified person's opinion on whether issues likely to influence prospects of economic extraction can be resolved with further work. Must comply with §§229.1300–1305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral reserve estimates (content and disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If included, describe key assumptions, parameters, and methods used to estimate mineral reserves and to convert indicated/measured resources into reserves; include estimates at a specific point of reference; provide estimates for all commodities including quantities, grade/quality, cut-off grades, and recoveries; round off appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut-off grades must be based on detailed analysis including a long-term price that provides a reasonable basis for project economic viability; disclose price and reasons for selection including time frame; classify reserves into probable and proven per §229.1302(e)(2); when reporting multiple commodity equivalents, disclose individual grades and conversion factors; provide opinion on how reserves could be materially affected by risk factors or changes to modifying factors. Must comply with §§229.1300–1305.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mining methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe current or proposed mining methods and reasons for selecting them as most suitable for the reserves under consideration, including geotechnical and hydrological models and other parameters relevant to mine designs and plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include production rates, expected mine life, mining unit dimensions, dilution and recovery factors; requirements for stripping, underground development and backfilling; required mining equipment fleet and personnel; and include at least one map of the final mine outline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and recovery methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe current or proposed mineral processing methods and reasons for selecting them as most suitable, including a description or flow sheet of any current or proposed process plant, throughput and design, equipment characteristics, and current or projected requirements for energy, water, materials and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If method, plant design, or other parameter has never been used commercially for this mineralization, the qualified person must justify why the approach will be successful. Instruction: if such methods are still under development and never used commercially, no mineral resources or reserves may be disclosed on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe required infrastructure for the project: roads, rail, port facilities, dams, dumps and leach pads, tailings disposal, power, water, pipelines, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one map showing the layout of the infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the market for the mine's products, including justification for demand or sales over the life of the mine (or length of cash flow projections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information on markets, agency relationships, results of market studies, commodity price projections, product valuation, market entry strategies, and product specifications; describe all material contracts required for development (mining, concentrating, smelting, refining, transport, hedging, forward sales), state which contracts are executed vs still negotiated, and for affiliated contracts discuss whether terms are arm's-length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental studies, permitting, and community negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe factors related to environmental compliance, permitting, and interactions with local individuals or groups relevant to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include results of environmental studies (baseline or impact), waste and tailings disposal plans, site monitoring and water management during operations and after closure, permitting requirements and application status, any required performance or reclamation bonds, plans/negotiations/agreements with local individuals or groups, mine closure plans and associated costs, qualified person's opinion on adequacy of plans, and commitments to local procurement and hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital and operating costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide estimates of capital and operating costs with major components in tabular form, explain and justify basis for cost estimates including contingency budgets, and state the accuracy level of the estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified person must assess accuracy by considering risks associated with specific engineering estimation methods and the accuracy of those methods in prior similar environments; accuracy must comply with §229.1302 (Item 1302).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe key assumptions, parameters, and methods used to demonstrate economic viability and provide all material assumptions including discount rates, exchange rates, commodity prices, taxes, royalties, and other applicable levies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose economic results including annual cash flow forecasts based on a production schedule, and measures such as NPV, IRR, and payback period; include sensitivity analysis for variants in commodity price, grade, costs, or other inputs and discuss impacts; if including economic analysis in an initial assessment, include a statement (equal prominence) that mineral resources do not have demonstrated economic viability; inferred resources may be included in economic analysis only if conditions in §229.1302(d)(4)(ii) are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjacent properties
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, a qualified person may include information concerning an adjacent property only if: the information was publicly disclosed by the owner/operator; the source is identified; the qualified person states they have been unable to verify the information and that it is not necessarily indicative of the subject property's mineralization; and the technical report summary clearly distinguishes adjacent property information from information about the subject property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly separate and source any adjacent-property material included and state verification limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other relevant data and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any additional information or explanation necessary to provide a complete and balanced presentation of the value of the property to the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information included must comply with §§229.1300–1305 (subpart 229.1300 of Regulation S-K).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified person must summarize interpretations and conclusions based on the data and analysis in the technical report summary, and discuss any significant risks and uncertainties that could reasonably be expected to affect reliability or confidence in exploration results, resource or reserve estimates, or projected economic outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide candid assessment of risks and uncertainties that materially affect confidence in the conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations (additional work and costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, describe recommended additional work with associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should be specific and include cost estimates to allow assessment of feasibility and planning for further work.
